newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds modestly up, market takes a breather.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds modestly up, market takes a breather.

text.p: Irish government bonds made further gains on Monday although trade was modest as the market took a breather after the previous week's frenetic advance, dealers said.

They said some short-term profit taking was possible, although the continued strength of the Irish pound would be supportive of the market. Irish credit growth and government borrowing data released later this week was also expected to be broadly supportive, they said.
"Foreign investors are not so prevalent today," one dealer said.

"The short end still seems popular and we've seen a bit more foreign buying of the shorts," he said. "But the 10-year area seems to have run into a bit of a wall for the moment at 90 (basis points) over Germany."
By 1540 GMT the eight percent bond due 2000 was up nine pence at 106.15 to yield 6.14 percent. The eight percent bond due 2006 was up 20p at 107.15 to yield 6.85 percent.
"We had phenomenal turnover last week and it's left the market a little hungover in terms of turnover today," a dealer said. "All European markets are seeing people pausing for breath a little bit."
Dealers said the 10-year spread over Germany was unlikely to narrow further until spreads at the shorter-end had narrowed.
"You'll have to see good narrowing of spreads in the shorts before the 10-year will go again," one said.

During the day the NTMA redeemed 71.4 million punts of the 8.5 percent bond due 1996 and 412.0 million of the variable-rate bond due 1996, and dealers said it was surprising that the National Treasury Management Agency (NTMA) had not announced a tap issue.

"A good chunk of cash has come in to the market today but there's still no sign of the NTMA rolling-over the debt. They are very comfortable with their funding position and this is probably the best explanation for their no-show to date," one said.
